Framework: Use OmniRec as the sole recommender-system framework for all loading, preprocessing, model training, evaluation, and reporting; do not call LensKit, RecBole, or other raw backend libraries directly.

Dataset scope: Use exactly three datasets with implicit feedback: MovieLens 100K, Amazon Video Games (VideoGames.csv), Hetrec LastFM (UserTaggedArtiststimestamps.dat); map to labels: MovieLens100K, AmazonVideoGames, HetrecLastFM.
Data location: Raw data located at ../../../study/data/; MovieLens data in u.data; Amazon Video Games in VideoGames.csv; Last.FM in UserTaggedArtiststimestamps.dat.
Preprocessing: Apply 5-core filtering to all datasets.

Implicit conversion: For MovieLens and Amazon datasets, convert any explicit rating > 3 to implicit interactions; preserve existing implicit interactions; for Last.FM dataset, convert to implicit interactions if not already implicit.
Holdout protocol: Generate 5 distinct random seeds for data splitting; perform a user-based 80/20 train/test split for each seed.
Algorithms: Evaluate ALS, ItemKNN, and Pop using OmniRec equivalents with the same semantics as LensKit 0.14.4.
Hyperparameters: Train all models using OmniRec's standard/default hyperparameters for each algorithm; no manual hyperparameter tuning beyond defaults; ensure identical defaults across datasets.
Evaluation metrics: Compute nDCG@1, nDCG@5, nDCG@10 and Precision@1, Precision@5, Precision@10 on the test set; use per-user aggregation to produce global metrics.

Statistical analysis: Conduct a short analysis to assess the impact of seed randomness on results (e.g., paired t-tests or non-parametric alternatives per dataset-algorithm across seeds) and report p-values and effect sizes.
Experimental design: For each dataset, algorithm, and seed, use a user-based 80/20 split; ensure train/test sizes are reasonable given data sparsity; maintain consistent split ratio across all runs.

Results and outputs: Save per-run metrics to a structured results store (CSV/JSON); generate plots per dataset-algorithm showing metric values across seeds for k=1,5,10; include box/violin plots of metric distributions across seeds; all plots saved as PNG/SVG in a report directory.

Plots: Produce at least three plot types per dataset-algorithm: (a) line plots of mean nDCG@k across seeds for k=1,5,10; (b) line plots of mean Precision@k across seeds for k=1,5,10; (c) box/violin plots of metric distributions across seeds; all plots saved as PNG/SVG in a report directory.
Reproducibility and logging: Record seed values, data splits, hyperparameters, and random state usage in a log file; timestamp results for traceability.
Output formats and destinations: Write a concise results summary file (CSV/JSON), and separate per-run result files; place plots and tables in a reproducible results directory.
Atomicity and constraints: Each requirement tests a single aspect of the experiment (data prep, splitting, model run, evaluation, statistics, plots, reproducibility).
